title: cognition-domains-general-coding-research
intention: Cognition domains: machines that sit above inference_domain and below devices, carrying escalation strategies and agentic loops. Three foreseeable: GENERAL (baseline LLM capabilities any device can use), CODING (specialized for code work, aider-like devices), RESEARCH (specialized for research, librarian graduates to this). Custom per-device domains based on a common one are allowed as experiments.
why: A device needs LLM smarts at different levels — the cairn device might use limited general-domain chat for support questions, while the aider shim needs a full coding domain with its own escalation. Without domains, every device reinvents its own escalation strategy. With them, the strategy is composed from a machine and the device can mix domains (general for help-desk, custom for core work) in the same device.
traces_to: Telos 1 — inference compilation: each domain compiles its own reasoning patterns.
Law 6 — gated ownership: each domain owns its escalation, a device composes but does not reach inside.
Design: cocoon-settle-stages-around-cc — domains ARE the cheaper stages.
Design: nexi-everywhere-hardware-ladder — LLM only to learn; fire-paths are hardware. Domains start with hand-coded escalation, LLM learns better parameters.

falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) a domain is a class hierarchy instead of a composed machine — inheritance forces a choice, composition allows mixing; (2) a device cannot use a domain for limited things without becoming LLM-heavy; (3) the general domain cannot serve as baseline for a device that doesn't need specialization; (4) a custom domain cannot override the common one's escalation strategy; (5) the domain's question list is not expressible as (question, owner) tuples in the embeddings generator.

children: emerge from design — at minimum: general-cognition-domain, coding-cognition-domain, research-cognition-domain as separate builds

questions.a: (1) A domain is COMPOSED, not inherited — a device can mix domains in the same device.
(2) The escalation strategy is the differentiator, not the models.
(3) Escalation and agentic loops can live in the domain OR the device — domain is default, device overrides for custom.
(4) A device can use a domain for limited things (cairn device: support questions) without being LLM-heavy.
(5) Custom per-device domains (experiments) are based on a common one.
(6) Progression: start general, graduate to specialized as the consumer matures.

how: A domain is a MACHINE in the complexity axis (tools + glue). The glue IS the escalation strategy — that is what differentiates domains, not the models they call. Domains are COMPOSED by devices, not inherited from — composition lets a device mix domains, inheritance forces a choice. The inference proxy already works this way (domain.resolve() is a call, not a class hierarchy). Each domain naturally owns its question list — connects to question-tree-embeddings-generator via the (question, owner) tuple design. Progression: a device starts on the general domain and graduates to a specialized one as it matures (librarian: general → research). The escalation and agentic loops can live in the domain OR the device — the domain is the default location, the device overrides when it needs custom behavior.
